features.claim: A tambourine is a percussion instrument made of a frame.
features.quote: The tambourine is a musical instrument in the percussion family consisting of a frame, often of wood or plastic, with pairs of small metal jingles, called "zills".

features.claim: The frame usually has pairs of small metal jingles set in it.
features.quote: The tambourine is a musical instrument in the percussion family consisting of a frame, often of wood or plastic, with pairs of small metal jingles, called "zills".

features.claim: The frame is often made of wood or plastic.

features.claim: The most common shape of a tambourine is round.
features.quote: Tambourines come in many shapes with the most common being circular.

features.claim: A tambourine usually has a drumhead, a skin stretched over it.
features.quote: Classically the term tambourine denotes an instrument with a drumhead, though some variants may not have a head.

features.claim: A tambourine looks like a small drum you can hold in your hand.
features.quote: The tambourine looks like a small hand-held drum.

features.claim: Besides the drumhead, it has small pairs of jingles like tiny cymbals set in slots around the frame.
features.quote: But in addition to the skin (drumhead) there are also small pairs of jingles - like tiny cymbals - in slots around the frame.

debated.claim: Some tambourines are made without a skin, so a picture may or may not show a drumhead.
debated.quote: Some are made without a skin, particularly for use in schools.

debated.claim: Not every tambourine has a drumhead, though the classic kind does.
